source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 20. Exercises reused from the lesson.
topic: Lady Khadijah, and the wise decision at the Ka'bah

learn.en: Khadijah, a noble and rich lady of Quraysh, heard of his honesty and asked him to lead her trade caravan to Syria. He came back successful every time.
learn.title: Khadijah's offer

learn.en: She saw his good character and proposed marriage. He was 25 and she was 40. They had two sons and four daughters.
learn.title: Marriage

learn.en: When the Ka'bah was rebuilt, the tribes argued for five days over who would place the Black Stone. They almost fought!
learn.title: The Black Stone

learn.en: They agreed the first man through the gate would decide. It was Muhammad ﷺ: “He is trustworthy — we accept his decision!”
learn.title: The first through the gate

learn.en: He put the stone on a cloth; every chief lifted a corner, then he placed it with his own hands. Everyone was happy. He was 35.
learn.title: A wise decision

learn.en: “There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example.” (Qur'an 33:21)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

quiz.en: Why did Khadijah want to marry him?
How many daughters did they have?
What did he use to lift the Black Stone?
True or false? Every tribe got a share of the honour of lifting the stone.

think.q: When two friends argue, how could you help, like the Prophet ﷺ did with the Black Stone?
think.a: Find a fair way where everyone shares — and everyone is happy.

parents.summary: He led Lady Khadijah's trade, married her, and at 35 solved the Black Stone dispute fairly with a cloth all the chiefs lifted.
parents.tip: Act out the Black Stone story with a tea towel and a ball.
